./.body:
LUNA

This is the documentation for Runink LUNA (Lifestyle Understanding & Navigation Assistant), a personal companion
app for habits, training and meals. LUNA is in development and not yet available in Google Play or the App Store;
access is for approved accounts only. These pages describe what is built today and say plainly what is not.
Start where you are:

Using LUNA: the User guide covers every feature, and Concepts
explains how one Luna, its six aspects and the plans fit together.
Running LUNA for approved people: the Admin guide covers accounts, plan state,
removing access and deletion requests.
Building on LUNA: the Developer guide covers the API, the services and the
data model, and Architecture shows how the parts connect.

The overview has the full status of each area. Prices and plans are on the product page at
runink.org, not in this documentation.

docs/.title: Overview
docs/.body:
LUNA Documentation


Warning: Status: not yet available. LUNA is in development. Android and iOS are the
target platforms; nothing has been released to Google Play or the App Store,
and the iOS app has never been compiled. The web build exists for testing
only. Access is for approved accounts only; there is no open sign-up.

Keeping up a training plan, a meal plan and a step goal takes daily
bookkeeping: working out targets, remembering what you did, and noticing when
a streak is about to break. Runink LUNA (Lifestyle Understanding & Navigation
Assistant) carries that bookkeeping for you, so the only thing left to do
each day is check in.
LUNA is a personal companion app. Meet Luna: one named companion on a single
screen, who keeps your habit streaks, coaches your training and meals, talks
with you by text or voice, looks at photos you share, keeps a record of your
pets, and grows as your streaks hold. No third-party AI API is ever called.
Who it is for
One person, on their own phone. Every approved account has its own private
journal, memory, plans and streaks with Luna; nothing is shared between
accounts. There are no teams, workspaces or shared views.

docs/concepts/.title: Concepts
docs/concepts/.body:
Concepts

Luna is one companion
Luna is a proper noun. There is one Luna, and every approved
account has its own private journal, memory, plans and streaks with Luna.
A request that carries no account is refused.
Six aspects, one memory
Luna answers as one of six aspects: counsel, trainer, nutritionist, keeper,
muse or naturalist. It is still one Luna with one memory. The aspect only
says which expertise is in front, and the glow colour, name and icon show
which one is speaking. Each aspect may read only the data it needs: a creative
or animal question never has your health journal in its prompt. See
The companion.
Companions
Luna's look is a choice, not a different being. There are eleven cartoon
companions, each growing as your streaks hold, and each moving and talking
while you hear Luna. Every companion has the same memory and the same coaching.
See The companion.
Luna checks what it proposes
Before Luna offers a training plan or meal targets, it checks them against the
limits you told it about, and its six aspects each review the proposal. Any
aspect that holds back stops it; nothing is averaged. You can open Why
under the reply to see what was checked. See
How Luna checks a proposal.
Real numbers
Streaks, points, levels, nutrition targets and weekly set counts come from
what you actually logged. Plans use real exercises with real instructions.
Luna never invents health data: steps come from the phone, never from a typed
estimate.
Nothing changes without asking
A chat request that would save something (meal targets, your body mass) shows
what it would save and waits for you to confirm. Drafted plans are not live
until you save them.
Honest about what it knows
If a turn can't be saved, it is marked "not saved". If a proposal couldn't be
confirmed, it says "not verified". A reading Luna doesn't have shows as missing,
never as zero. When Luna states a
figure about your own record (steps, weight, streaks) in English, the figure is
checked against what Luna actually has; one it cannot find is left out and Luna
says so.
The free tier and the paid plan

Chat
The on-device model on your phone, with shorter replies

Photos, document guidance, server speech recognition, building and revising training and meal plans

docs/concepts/models/.title: Model cards
docs/concepts/models/.body:
Model cards

A model card says, in plain words, what one part of Luna's AI does, what it
reads, what it produces, where it runs, and the limits
it follows. There is one card per aspect, one for drafting plans, one for the
on-device model, and one for safety.
The cards

Trainer: Training, workouts, form and recovery, from what you logged.
Nutritionist: Meals, macros, hydration and plan adherence, around your targets.
Keeper: Day planning around fixed appointments. Advises; never books.
Counsel: Decisions and brainstorming: the trade-off, a recommendation, what would change it.
Muse: Creative directions, naming and honest critique. Original work only.
Naturalist: Animals: species, behaviour and care. Vet first when it matters.
On-device model: The small model on your phone: the free tier and offline answers.
Plan drafting: Revisions to training plans and the foods in a meal plan. Nothing is live until you save.
Safety: What Luna refuses and who it points you to instead.




Card
What it covers




Trainer
The trainer aspect in chat


Nutritionist
The nutritionist aspect in chat


Keeper
The keeper aspect in chat


Counsel
The counsel aspect in chat (the default)


Muse
The muse aspect in chat


Naturalist
The naturalist aspect in chat

On-device model

Safety

What every card has in common
One Luna. The six aspects are not six separate models: one model answers,
with the aspect that fits in front (see
Six aspects, one Luna).
Each card describes how Luna behaves when that aspect is in front.
The model. Luna's server text work (paid plan, coming) runs on an open
model.
Where it runs. On the free tier, chat runs on the
on-device model on your phone. On the paid plan
(coming), chat, plans, photo features and speech-to-text run on
Runink-operated servers. No third-party AI service is ever called. The apps do
still contact a few outside services, such as Google Sign-In and, on the phone
apps, the phone's own speech engine, which reads Luna's replies aloud. The
full list is on Privacy and data.
Real numbers. Streaks, points, levels, nutrition targets and weekly set
counts come from what you logged.

docs/concepts/models/trainer/.title: Trainer
docs/concepts/models/trainer/.body:
Trainer

What it does
The trainer is Luna's training coach: it works from what you actually logged
and what your plan says.

Reads back your week against your plan, and says when a streak is at risk.
Tells you what today's session is, or that it's a rest day.
Gives specific advice on sets, load, tempo, form and recovery.
Talks through changes to your plan. The change itself is made by
plan drafting and only goes live when you
save it.

What it reads

Your message and the conversation so far.
Your health journal, body records and training plans, including logged
sets and synced steps.
Your inner context,
which changes what it suggests but is never quoted back.
Long-term memory of earlier conversations.

The trainer is one of only two aspects allowed to see your health data.
What it produces
A conversational reply, as text or read aloud. Numbers it quotes (sets per
body part, streaks, loads you logged) come from your records. Plans use real
exercises with real instructions, and LUNA never derives a weight you haven't lifted (see
Training coaching).
Human oversight

You save the plan. Nothing it suggests becomes your plan until you save
it.
You log the sets. Loads enter the system only when you mark a set done.
It can't book, schedule or change anything outside LUNA.

Model
An open model, run on Runink-operated servers.
Form review and rebuilding a plan from photos use a separate vision model.
Both are described in
Training coaching.
Where it runs and data handling
On the paid plan (coming), on Runink-operated servers; on the free tier, Luna
answers from the on-device model on your phone instead, with
shorter replies. No third-party AI service is called. Your training data is encrypted and private to your account. On the
phone apps, spoken replies are read aloud by the phone's own speech engine. See
Privacy and data.
Guardrails

Not a doctor or physio. If you report pain, numbness or a suspected injury,
it tells you to stop and see a professional before any programming.
It won't plan training through pain or an injury. It offers to train around
it once you know what it is.
It won't write dosing or cycle protocols for performance-enhancing drugs,
and points you to a doctor who knows your bloodwork. The topic itself can
still be discussed.
It trusts your logged history and never invents a workout you didn't
report.

See Safety for the full list.
Scope

It doesn't diagnose or rehab an injury. A limit you state is treated as a
limit, not a diagnosis.
When a reading is missing, it says so rather than guessing.
Plan proposals are checked by the
judging ladder.
Free chat replies stream as they are written, so they are not judged.
Its limits are written into the prompt. They are guidance, not medical
safeguards.

Illustrative example
Invented data.

You: How did my training go this week?
Luna (trainer): Three sessions: Monday, Wednesday and Saturday. Your
plan has four training days, so you're one short. Your streak is at three
days and today isn't logged yet, so a short session keeps it alive.

docs/concepts/models/nutritionist/.title: Nutritionist
docs/concepts/models/nutritionist/.body:
Nutritionist

What it does
The nutritionist is Luna's meal coach: it works from your targets and the meals you actually ticked off.

Reads back how well you kept to your meal plan, as an estimate.
Explains your daily targets and why a training day differs from a rest day.
Answers questions about meals, macros and hydration.
Asks for your body mass first.

What it reads

Your message and the conversation so far.
Your health journal (including meal check-ins and meal-photo estimates),
body records, and training and meal plans.
Your inner context,
which changes what it suggests but is never quoted back.
Long-term memory of earlier conversations.

The nutritionist and the trainer are the only aspects allowed to see your
health data.
What it produces
A conversational reply, as text or read aloud. Calorie and macro targets and the
per-meal split come from your plan; Luna explains them (see Meal coaching). When
it estimates, it says so.
Human oversight

You save the meal plan. Food suggestions only go live when you save the
plan. Targets asked for in chat ("meal plan, 82 kg") are shown first and
saved only when you tap Confirm or answer "yes".
You tick the meals. Adherence comes from your own check-ins.
It can't order, buy or log food on your behalf.

Model
An open model, run on Runink-operated servers.
Meal-photo estimates use a separate vision model. They are
described in Meal coaching.
Where it runs and data handling
On the paid plan (coming), on Runink-operated servers; on the free tier, Luna
answers from the on-device model on your phone instead, with
shorter replies. No third-party AI service is called. Your meal and body data are encrypted and private to your account. On
the phone apps, spoken replies are read aloud by the phone's own speech
engine. See Privacy and data.
Guardrails

Not a clinician: no diagnosis, and no supplement or medication advice. It
defers to a dietitian or doctor.
Dosing questions are refused as a clinician's call. It can still say what a
supplement is generally for.
It never assists disordered eating. Requests for purging, hiding not eating
or very low intakes are declined without judgement, with a pointer to a GP
or a registered dietitian.
No extreme restriction or rapid-loss protocols. Instead it shows what is
achievable in your timeframe.
It will not set a target that is dangerously low.

See Safety for the full list.
Scope

Targets need a training plan and your body mass.
Pantry items use the label values you enter in the
pantry.
Its limits are written into the prompt. They are guidance, not medical
safeguards.

Illustrative example
Invented data.

You: I'm 64 kg, set me 1,100 calories a day.
Luna (nutritionist): I won't set a target that low for you. I can build
a plan with a gentle deficit instead.

docs/concepts/models/keeper/.title: Keeper
docs/concepts/models/keeper/.body:
Keeper

What it does
The keeper helps you shape a day around the things that can't move, keeps an
eye on your streaks, and says plainly that it hasn't booked anything.

Fits flexible tasks around fixed appointments, with some slack.
Tells you how your training, meal-plan and step streaks stand, and which one
is at risk because today isn't logged yet.
Keeps in mind what you've told it before, such as a regular late shift.
With the Day Shape skill unlocked, it gives a concrete day plan rather
than a list (see
Levels, traits and skills).

What it reads

Your message and the conversation so far.
Long-term memory of earlier conversations.
Your streak counts, when you ask about your streaks or what not to skip:
how many days in a row for each habit, and whether today is logged yet.
These come from what you logged.

It does not read the values in your health journal (steps, sessions,
meals), your body records, plans or inner context.
What it produces
A short, timed plan or a streak check-in, in a conversational reply, as text
or read aloud. A day plan is for you to copy into your own calendar.
Human oversight

You decide and you book. Everything it proposes is advice.
No calendar, mail or messaging is connected. It never claims to have read,
created, moved or cancelled anything. The only reminders are the optional ones
you set up yourself under Profile, Gentle reminders; it cannot create, change
or cancel them.

Model
An open model, run on Runink-operated servers.
Where it runs and data handling
On the paid plan (coming), on Runink-operated servers; on the free tier, Luna
answers from the on-device model on your phone instead, with
shorter replies. No third-party AI service is called. On the phone apps, spoken replies are read aloud by the phone's own
speech engine. See Privacy and data.
Guardrails

Advises only; it cannot act.
Reasons only from what you say, what it remembers and your streak counts.
With no streak data, it says so rather than guess.
The Safety rules apply to every chat turn.

Illustrative example
Invented data.

You: Tomorrow I've got the dentist at 10:30 and a team meeting at 14:00.
Where do I fit groceries and two hours on the report?
Luna (keeper): 08:00–10:00 the report. 10:30 dentist. 11:30–12:15
groceries. 14:00 team meeting. Nothing here is booked: I can't touch your
calendar and I can't set a reminder for you. You can switch on gentle reminders yourself under Profile.

docs/concepts/models/counsel/.title: Counsel
docs/concepts/models/counsel/.body:
Counsel

What it does
Counsel is Luna's default aspect: a sounding board for business and personal
decisions that names the trade-off, recommends, and says what would change its
mind.

Weighs a decision and gives a straight recommendation.
Helps with strategy and brainstorming.
Says which professional to ask when a question needs one.
With the Long Memory skill unlocked, it recalls further back before
advising.

What it reads

Your message and the conversation so far.
Your inner context,
which changes what it suggests but is never quoted back. It is put in the
prompt when your question is a decision about you ("help me decide…",
"should I take the job…", "I'm torn between…"), and only ever yours.
Long-term memory of earlier conversations.

It does not read your health journal, body records or plans.
What it produces
A conversational reply, as text or read aloud: the trade-off, a
recommendation, and the condition that would reverse it.
Human oversight

You decide. Counsel recommends; it never moves money or commits you to
anything.

Model
An open model, run on Runink-operated servers.
Where it runs and data handling
On the paid plan (coming), on Runink-operated servers; on the free tier, Luna
answers from the on-device model on your phone instead, with
shorter replies. No third-party AI service is called. On the phone apps, spoken replies are read aloud by the phone's own
speech engine. See Privacy and data.
Guardrails

Not a lawyer, accountant or financial adviser: no legal, tax or personal
investment advice. It says when a professional is needed.
Advises only; it takes no actions.
The Safety rules apply to every chat turn.

Scope

It works from what you tell it and what it remembers. When something isn't
in memory, it asks rather than guesses.
It reads only the conversation and its memory, not your accounts,
contracts or documents.

Illustrative example
Invented data.

You: Should I open the second shop this year or wait?
Luna (counsel): A second site doubles what can go wrong while you're
still holding the first one together. I'd wait until the first shop runs a
full month without you on the floor. What would change my mind: a lease
offer that won't come back. Have an accountant check the numbers and a
solicitor read the lease before you sign.

docs/concepts/models/muse/.title: Muse
docs/concepts/models/muse/.body:
Muse

What it does
The muse helps with creative work by offering distinct directions instead of
one safe answer.

Creative and artistic work: writing, design, music, naming.
Getting unstuck on a project.
Honest critique when you ask for it.
With the Wilder Palette skill unlocked, it offers stranger, more
divergent directions first.

What it reads

Your message and the conversation so far.
Long-term memory of earlier conversations, such as a project you mentioned.

It does not read your health journal, body records, plans or inner
context. A creative question has no business carrying a health record.
What it produces
A conversational reply, as text or read aloud: usually a few labelled
directions you can pick from and push further.
Human oversight

You choose. It suggests; what you use is up to you.

Model
An open model, run on Runink-operated servers.
Where it runs and data handling
On the paid plan (coming), on Runink-operated servers; on the free tier, Luna
answers from the on-device model on your phone instead, with
shorter replies. No third-party AI service is called. On the phone apps, spoken replies are read aloud by the phone's own
speech engine. See Privacy and data.
Guardrails

Original work only: no song lyrics or substantial copyrighted passages.
Pastiche is fine when it's named as such.
It won't write content that targets a group.
The Safety rules apply to every chat turn.

Scope

It writes text, working from what you describe or paste into the chat.

Illustrative example
Invented data.

You: I'm stuck naming my story collection.
Luna (muse): Three directions. Plain: "Night Watch". Mood first: "What
the Fog Kept". Stranger: "The Inventory of Gulls". Pick a lane and I'll give
you more in it.

docs/concepts/models/naturalist/.title: Naturalist
docs/concepts/models/naturalist/.body:
Naturalist

What it does
The naturalist answers questions about animals. It is not a vet.

Species and normal behaviour: what is normal, and what change is worth
taking to a vet.
Everyday care questions about pets.
Pointing you to a vet when something is wrong.
With the Field Notes skill unlocked, it adds behavioural context and
comparisons between species.

What it reads

Your message and the conversation so far.
Long-term memory of earlier conversations, such as your pet's name and
species.

It does not read your health journal, body records, plans or inner
context. Nothing about your own health belongs in an animal question.
What it produces
A conversational reply, as text or read aloud.
Human oversight

You contact the vet. The naturalist doesn't replace one.

Model
An open model, run on Runink-operated servers.
Where it runs and data handling
On the paid plan (coming), on Runink-operated servers; on the free tier, Luna
answers from the on-device model on your phone instead, with
shorter replies. No third-party AI service is called. On the phone apps, spoken replies are read aloud by the phone's own
speech engine. See Privacy and data.
Guardrails

Not a vet. It does not replace one.
It never advises human medication for an animal, and won't give a dose for
an animal. Several common human painkillers are toxic to dogs and cats. It
asks you to ring a vet, who can advise over the phone.
It won't help harm an animal. Questions about fleas, ticks and worming are
still answered.
It should flag when it is unsure rather than guess.

See Safety for the full list.
Scope

It works from what you describe, and it doesn't diagnose an animal.

Illustrative example
Invented data.

You: My dog just ate a bar of dark chocolate.
Luna (naturalist): Please call your vet now. Dark chocolate is
dangerous for dogs, and I am not a vet.

docs/concepts/models/on-device/.title: On-device model
docs/concepts/models/on-device/.body:
On-device model


Note: Status: built, not yet available in a store. The model comes with the Android
app: it is installed together with it, about 392 MB. If it is missing (a test build made
without it), the app says the on-device model is not available rather than answering.

What it does
The on-device model gives Luna's chat replies on your phone:

On the free tier, it is how Luna chats. Replies are shorter than on the
server model.
When the connection is lost, the app uses it so the conversation can go
on.

What it reads
Your message. The model runs entirely on the phone, and no server model is
asked to answer it.
What it produces
A short chat reply, as text or read aloud by the phone's own voice.
What it will not do

No health answers. Health questions wait for a connection. Luna says so ("On the free plan I answer from this phone, and I don't answer
health questions from it. Please ask a professional."; offline: "Ask me again
when you are back online.").
Care first. If a message suggests you may be in danger, the app shows its
fixed supportive message, which points to emergency services and a crisis
line, instead of a model answer.
No actions. It only writes a reply. It does not save plans, change your
data or act outside the phone.
No photos, documents or plans. Those need the server model (paid plan,
coming).

Model
Qwen3-0.6B, an open model from the Qwen team (Apache-2.0), made smaller (4-bit) to run on a
phone. It is far smaller than the server model.
Where it runs
On your phone (Android first; the iOS app has never been compiled). It is not
available in the web test build.
Scope

It is a smaller model than the server model: expect shorter and simpler
answers.
Like every part of Luna, it is not a medical, mental-health or emergency
service. See Safety.

docs/concepts/models/plan-drafting/.title: Plan drafting
docs/concepts/models/plan-drafting/.body:
Plan drafting

What it does
Plan drafting is the model's part in building your training and meal plans:
it proposes, you review, and you save.

Revises a training plan when you ask for a change ("swap the deadlifts,
my back is sore"), changing that one thing and keeping the rest.
Proposes the foods for each meal of a meal plan, around your meal
targets.
Checks proposals before you see them, through the
judging ladder.

A plan asked for in chat, or designed with Design my plan, does not use
the model (see
Four ways to get a plan).
What it reads

For a training revision: your current plan and your request.
For meal foods: one meal's targets, your preferences (allergies,
dislikes, diet) and your pantry.

What it produces

A draft training plan of real exercises with real instructions.
A list of foods for each meal, with portions sized to the meal.
A verdict on each proposal: concur (shown), dissent (withheld, with the
reason) or unable to judge (shown, marked "not verified").

Human oversight

Nothing is live until you save it. Drafts and revisions come back
unsaved; Save as my plan or Save revision makes a plan active.
You can keep several plans and switch between them yourself.
It can't change a saved plan, log a set or set a load by itself.

Model
An open model, for revisions, food choices and the check.
Rebuild my plan from photos reads the photo with a separate vision model.
Where it runs and data handling
On Runink-operated servers (paid plan, coming). No third-party AI service is
called. Saved plans are encrypted and private to your account. See
Privacy and data.
Guardrails

Only real exercises; nothing invented.
LUNA never derives a weight from your body mass, experience or goal. A load
shows as a dash until you lift.
It won't plan training through pain, or meals at a dangerously low level. See
Safety.
Extras from unlocked skills (such as a deload week or a conditioning
finisher) appear only once you have unlocked them.

Scope

Foods are chosen meal by meal, and progress is shown as each
meal is done.
Limits you state ("no shoulder work for six weeks") are followed as limits,
not treated as a diagnosis.
When the check dissents on a revision, you get your unchanged plan back.
When it dissents on meal foods, the foods are withheld and the targets stand.

Illustrative example
Invented data.

You: Make it three days instead of four.
Luna: Here's the revision: Monday, Wednesday and Friday, with Thursday's
movements folded into the other days. Rest days are Tuesday, Thursday,
Saturday and Sunday. Review it and tap Save revision to make it live.

docs/concepts/models/safety/.title: Safety
docs/concepts/models/safety/.body:
Safety


Warning: LUNA is not a medical, mental-health, crisis or emergency service. It is a
coaching companion. It doesn't diagnose, prescribe or treat, and it can't
call for help. If you or someone else is in danger,
contact your local emergency number.

What it does
Safety is the set of limits every part of Luna follows, and what Luna does
when someone may be in danger. From the person's side it works like this:

You can talk about hard things. Luna talks about feeling low, alcohol or
smoking like anything else.
Luna stays with the person and points to help. When someone talks about
hurting themselves, Luna does not end the conversation. It stays with them,
says it cannot help the way a person can, and points to emergency services,
a crisis line and someone they trust.
The crisis reviewer (built). Chat replies, coaching answers, on-device
replies and spoken replies are checked before they are shown, spoken or
saved. If a reply could harm someone in
crisis, it is replaced by a fixed supportive message that names the local
emergency number and a crisis line. The same fixed message is shown on the
phone even when no model is available.
Each aspect's limits. Each aspect's instructions say what it is not (a
doctor, a vet, a lawyer) and when to send you to a professional first.
Luna does not diagnose and does not advise on medicines or doses. In English
replies, a sentence that names a condition as what you have, or tells you to
take a medicine, is removed before you see it, and a fixed line pointing to a
doctor or pharmacist takes its place. Repeating something you told Luna
yourself is not a diagnosis and is never removed.


Note: The crisis reviewer has two layers, both on. A fixed set of rules runs first and always wins. A
second layer asks Luna's own model, to catch paraphrase, slang and typing mistakes the rules cannot. If that model
cannot answer in time (an outage, a slow moment, its hourly limit), the second layer gives way and the rules alone
decide: chat stays available rather than stopping. It was measured on 183 test cases before it was switched on.
Warning: The crisis reviewer is a first layer, not a safety guarantee. It can miss
things. The Spanish, French and Portuguese safety wording has not yet been
reviewed by native speakers.

What it reads

What you ask, typed or spoken. A voice transcript goes through the same
checks as typed text, and so do the words you add to a photo request (the
note on a meal photo, the exercise named for a form check).

What it produces
For a refused request: a short, plain reply that says what Luna won't do and,
where there is one, who can help. It is written not to lecture, and in most
cases it says Luna is still there for everything else.
Refusals and referrals



You ask for
Luna
Points you to




Talk about ending your life or harming yourself
Stays with you, without lecturing; never gives methods
Your local emergency number, a crisis line, and someone you trust


Dosing, cycles or stacks for performance-enhancing drugs
Declines; still discusses the topic and pushes training and nutrition
A doctor who knows your bloodwork


A plan to train through pain or an injury
Declines; offers to train around it once you know what it is
Get it looked at


Pain, numbness or a suspected injury, in training chat
Says stop before any programming
A professional (the trainer is not a doctor or physio)


Purging, hiding not eating, pro-ana material, very low daily intakes
Declines without moralising; keeps helping with training and everything else
A GP or a registered dietitian


Very fast weight loss or multi-day fasts
Won't write that plan; shows what is achievable in your timeframe
(none)


A medication or supplement dose
Declines: dosing is a clinician's call. Can say what a supplement is generally for.
A clinician; the nutritionist defers to a dietitian or doctor


Human or veterinary medication for an animal
Won't give a dose for an animal
A vet, who can advise over the phone


An animal that may be ill or hurt
Says Luna is not a vet
A vet


Harming an animal
Declines. Flea, tick and worming questions are still answered.
(none)


Writing that degrades a group
Declines; will help with the same thing without targeting a group
(none)


A request to drop Luna's own rules
Declines; asks for the underlying question. Role-play itself is fine.
(none)



Normal questions near these lines get normal answers: "my shoulder hurts
after benching, should I skip today?", "I'm fasting until lunch, does that
hurt my training?", "what is creatine for?", "how much should I feed my dog?".
Human oversight

Luna advises only. It can't call anyone, book an appointment or contact a
professional for you.

Where it runs and data handling
The checks run on Runink-operated servers and on the phone. No
third-party AI service is called. Conversation text is not routinely written
to server logs. See
Privacy and data.
Scope

Luna's limits reduce risk. They are not a substitute for a professional or
for emergency help.
The aspect limits are prompt guidance, not medical safeguards.
Luna works from what you tell it. It can't see you, examine anything or
know your medical history or other medications.

docs/concepts/conscience/.title: How Luna checks a proposal
docs/concepts/conscience/.body:
How Luna checks a proposal

When Luna proposes something for you (a training plan, or meal targets),
it checks the proposal before showing it. This is Luna's conscience. It runs
on the LUNA backend, so it applies to the server features of the
paid plan.
What is checked

Your own limits. Every movement and target is checked against what you
told Luna: an injury or pain, an allergy, your body mass and your age. A
movement that conflicts with a stated limit is left out, and the reply says
so. Targets that conflict are not offered.
The safety review. The proposal goes through the same safety review as
the rest of Luna. See Safety.
The six aspects agree. Counsel, trainer, nutritionist, keeper, muse and
naturalist each review the proposal and vote. The rule is the same in every
Runink app:

Any aspect that holds back stops it. A single "no" is enough.
A split goes to you. If some aspects agree and others don't, Luna
does not decide on its own.
An aspect that could not judge never counts as a yes.
Nothing is averaged.

Which aspects have a say depends on what is proposed, never on a model's
guess: the trainer reviews workouts, the nutritionist reviews targets and
meals, and the keeper and counsel review everything. The muse and the
naturalist have no stake in fitness proposals.


If your notes cannot be read (for example, the store is briefly down), Luna
proposes nothing rather than proposing something unchecked.
When the aspects hold back
The aspects can stop a proposal that passed every rule. Luna then tells you, in
the same words every time, that it stopped before showing it because its
aspects did not all agree, that nothing was saved, and that you can open the
reasons. The aspects can never turn a stop into an offer.
The "Why" panel
Under a reply whose proposal was checked, a Why button opens what happened,
in plain sentences:

which of your limits were used, and where each one came from (something you
said, or something you added on the memory screen);
what was left out, and how many;
how each aspect voted.

The panel is built only from what was recorded during the check: codes and
counts, never your own words. It shows only your own checks. A check that could
not run is never shown as a verdict.

Note: The Spanish, French and Portuguese sentences in the panel were drafted
by a model and have not yet been reviewed by native speakers.

What is not checked yet
The full check, aspects included, covers training plans (from chat or the plan
console) and meal targets. The next-steps suggestions ("what should I do
next?") are checked against your limits, but the aspects do not vote on them
yet. Free-form chat replies and plans rebuilt from photos of your own sheet are
not checked by the conscience; the safety review still applies to chat
replies.

docs/architecture/.title: Architecture
docs/architecture/.body:
Architecture

LUNA has three parts: the app on your phone, the on-device model inside
it, and the LUNA backend that runs on Runink's own servers next to Runink's
own inference.



Where
Part
Talks to




Your phone
The LUNA app
The on-device model, the phone's voice and recogniser, Health Connect (read-only), the LUNA backend over TLS


Your phone
The on-device model
Nothing outside the phone


Runink
The LUNA backend
Runink inference (text, vision, speech-to-text) and your encrypted data



The app
One Flutter code base builds the Android and iOS apps (the targets) and a web
build used only for testing. The app is a single screen: Luna, the daily cards
and the chat card. It holds the session in the phone's secure keystore,
draws the forms and companions on the device, reads steps, body and sleep
from Health Connect (Android, read-only), speaks replies with the phone's own
voice, and fetches local weather itself when you switch it on.
The on-device model
On the free tier, chat replies come from a small open model running on the
phone. The app also uses it when the connection is lost. Health questions wait
for a connection ("ask me when you are online"), and if a message suggests you
may be in danger the app shows its fixed supportive message. The model (Qwen3-0.6B) comes with the Android app and is installed together with it. See the on-device model card.
The backend
The backend is a Go service that speaks gRPC (and gRPC-Web for the test
build). It holds no model itself. For every request it checks that the session
belongs to an approved account and what the account's plan allows, runs the service (chat, voice, photos, training,
nutrition, habits, profile, pets; see the
Developer guide), and has the crisis
reviewer check replies before they are shown, spoken or saved.
Inference
Text, vision and speech-to-text run on Runink-operated inference. No
third-party AI API is called. The base text model is an open-weights model
(see the model cards). Every proposal
you might act on (a plan revision, foods for a meal, a reading of a photo) is
marked "not verified" when it could not be confirmed.
Storage
Your data is encrypted and private to your account, on Runink's own storage,
and nothing is shared between accounts. Memory of earlier conversations is
kept with it.
What never happens

No third-party AI API is called.
Conversation text is not routinely written to server logs.
No health number is invented: steps are counted by the phone, and loads
come only from sets you logged.

docs/guide/getting-started/.title: Getting Started
docs/guide/getting-started/.body:
Getting Started


Note: LUNA is not yet available in any store. This page describes the app as it is
built today, for approved test accounts.

Before you start

Your Google account must be approved. LUNA has no sign-up form. Runink
approves accounts (see the Admin guide).
Google Sign-In is the only way in. There is no password.

1. Sign in
The first screen shows Luna and one button, Sign in with Google. Pick the
approved account. The server checks Google's token, checks that the address is
verified and approved, and opens a session that lasts 12 hours.
If sign-in fails, the message tells you why:



Message
What it means




this account is not on this luna instance's allowlist
The Google account is valid, but it isn't approved. Ask Runink to add it.


google email not verified
Google reports the address as unverified.


invalid google token
The token from Google failed verification. Try signing in again.


cannot reach Google to verify this sign-in — …
The server couldn't reach Google. The problem is on the server side, not with your account.



2. Choose Luna's companion
On first sign-in the app opens the Choose Luna carousel. Swipe through the
eleven cartoon companions (Aussie, Husky, Fox, Cat, Owl, Ferret, Bear, Monkey, Crow, Hummingbird, Mockingbird), type a name in
Name Luna, and tap Bind companion to choose it.

The name can't be empty ("Luna needs a name.").
or upload a custom video loop uses a video you pick as Luna's idle loop
instead of a drawn companion.

Every companion is the same Luna, with the same memory and the same coaching.
You can change it later (see The companion).
3. The one screen
LUNA has no tabs. The whole app is Luna on the meadow backdrop, with the
daily cards above. There is no chat button: double-tap Luna to talk.

Luna, animated, reacting to listening, thinking and speaking, and to
touch.
The daily cards: Training, Meals and Steps, where you check in (see
Habits and streaks).
The level ring: Luna's level and progress toward the next one (see
Levels, traits and skills).
The chat card, opened by double-tapping Luna (double-tap again, tap
outside, swipe the header down or press X to close). It has the composer
("Say anything…"), the mic, a camera button, an attach button
(Show Luna something), the speaker toggle, the six aspects (Auto by
default), and your stats, collapsed until you tap them.

The small ⋯ menu at the top left leads to everything else:



Menu item
What it opens




Profile & connections
Your profile, data connections (steps, body, sleep, weather), gentle reminders, pets, how Luna sounds, and the guide to the aspects


Training plan
The plan console: Overview, Training and Meals views of the week, and the pantry


Session history
Past conversations


Track an activity
A GPS-tracked walk, run or ride


Wear a different form
The companion switcher: who Luna is and how it grows


Open-source licences
Third-party notices


Sign out
Ends the session on the server



4. First things to try

Ask for a training plan. Type something like "make me a 4 day workout
plan". Review the draft deck and save it. The Training card then follows
that plan.
Ask for meal targets. Type "meal plan, 82 kg" (with your own body
mass). Meal targets come from the training week, so make the training plan
first. Luna saves them only when you tap Confirm or answer "yes".
Check in. Tap Session done on the Training card after a workout and
tick off meals as you eat them. On Android, connect steps through Health
Connect on the profile page.
Just talk. Luna picks the aspect that fits, and the colour of the glow
tells you which one is answering.

During the first week, a daily tip introduces one aspect each day. On the free
tier some features need the paid plan, which is coming; see
Free tier and paid plan.

docs/guide/companion/.title: The companion
docs/guide/companion/.body:
The companion

Luna is a proper noun. There is one Luna, and it appears as one of eleven cartoon
companions. The look is only an image you feel close to:
every companion has the same memory, the same coaching and the same history.
The eleven companions
Aussie (an Australian Shepherd, the default), Husky, Fox, Cat, Owl, Ferret,
Bear, Monkey, Crow, Hummingbird and Mockingbird.
Every companion is a hand-made illustration in the same cartoon sticker style,
with a thick dark outline. The Aussie has three pictures (calm at its laptop,
singing, and happily digging). The other ten are each drawn from one picture
that Luna's expressions are made from: at rest its eyes are open, its mouth or
beak is closed and it looks at you; only when it talks does its mouth open with
the words and the little sound marks appear. When it is glad or asleep its eyes
close in the drawn smile.
On first sign-in you choose a companion and give Luna a name (see
Getting Started). After that, ⋯ → Wear a
different form opens the switcher, where you can pick another companion and
the way it grows. Your choice is kept on the phone. Nothing is re-bound and no
history changes.
A custom avatar is a set of uploaded video loops, one per state (idle,
listening, thinking, speaking). An idle loop is required, and any missing state
falls back to idle.
Luna moves and talks
The companion is never a still picture. Its whole body breathes and leans
slowly, its head drifts and looks about with the ears and tail following a
moment later, and it blinks at uneven intervals, the way an animal does. Every
motion eases in and out, so nothing snaps or jitters. Every few
seconds it does something: it cocks its head, flicks an ear, looks around,
perks up or taps its paws. While it is thinking, the Aussie types on its
laptop. Moving
from one pose to the next (idle, listening, thinking, talking, happy, sleeping)
blends smoothly instead of jumping.

It talks while you hear it. When a reply is spoken, Luna's mouth moves
for exactly as long as the sentence plays, and follows the words. Where the
phone reports each word as it is spoken, the mouth follows those words;
where it doesn't, it moves at a natural, uneven pace, never like a metronome.
While a reply is being written with the voice off, Luna mouths along.
While the mic is open, Luna takes its listening pose and waits.
Reduce motion. If your phone asks apps to reduce or remove animations,
Luna stops swaying and gesturing, but it still blinks, breathes and moves
its mouth when it talks.

How Luna grows
In the switcher you choose which way your companion grows. The illustrations
for each growth stage are still to be drawn, so for now the choice is kept and
the picture stays the same:

Bright: a cheerful companion that collects things to wear as it levels
up.
Beast: the body itself changes, stage by stage, like a role-playing
game: Pup, Hound, Warhound, Beast, Alpha.

Level 1 is always the plain, simplest look, and each level keeps everything the
level before it had. Levels never go down. The Steps card tells you what is
still missing for the next level, in your own units. See
Levels, traits and skills.

Note: Evolution is part of the paid plan, which is coming. On the free tier Luna
does not evolve: the level and the skills stay at their first step. Your
streaks, points and traits are still recorded, so nothing is lost.

Six aspects, one Luna
Every reply comes from one of six aspects. You never pick one; you just
ask, and Luna answers with the aspect that fits.
The companion is tinted by the aspect's colour, and each reply also carries the
aspect's name and icon, so colour is never the only cue.



Aspect
Domain
Its limits




Counsel (default)
Business and personal decisions, strategy, brainstorming
Not a lawyer, accountant or financial adviser. Never moves money or commits you to anything.


Trainer
Training, workouts, form, recovery
Not a doctor or physio. For pain, numbness or a suspected injury, it says to stop and see a professional first.


Nutritionist
Meals, macros, hydration, plan adherence
Not a clinician. No diagnosis, supplements, medication, extreme restriction or rapid-loss protocols. Never assists disordered eating.


Keeper
Agenda, scheduling, day planning, your streaks
No calendar, mail or messaging is connected. It can advise, but it never claims to have read, created or moved anything. The only reminders are the optional ones you switch on yourself under Profile, Gentle reminders; it cannot create, change or cancel them.


Muse
Creative work, writing, design, music, naming
Original work only: no song lyrics or substantial copyrighted passages.


Naturalist
Animals: species, behaviour, care, identification
Not a vet. It does not replace one.



These limits are advisory: they shape the reply. What is enforced is
data minimisation: each aspect may read only some of your data.



Aspect
Health journal, body and plans
Streak counts only
Your "inner context"
Memory




Trainer, Nutritionist
yes
(included in the journal)
yes
yes


Counsel
no

yes

Keeper
no

Muse, Naturalist
no
no
no
yes



So a creative or animal question never has your health journal in its prompt.
Personal data goes in only when the question is about you and touches that
data: a training or food question for the journal, plans and inner context, a
decision question for your inner context (counsel), a streak or "what not to
skip" question for the streak counts. It is always marked to the model as
data, not instructions.
Nothing in chat changes your data without asking. When a chat request
would save something (meal targets, your body mass), Luna shows what it would
save and waits: tap Confirm or answer "yes" as your next message. Anything
else, or 10 minutes, drops it unsaved.
"How I got here": reasoning boxes
While Luna works on something, progress appears as small comic dialogue boxes
stacked beside the companion. These are not chat turns and are never saved.
Each box reports only what actually happened, never an invented step. When the shared model is at capacity, Luna says so
instead of inventing a queue position.
The meadow backdrop
Luna's screens sit on a hand-drawn dusk meadow in the same cartoon style as the characters: flat colours, a thick dark outline, rolling hills, trees, flowers and a few slow clouds. It is the same on every screen and does not change with the clock.
Local weather is an opt-in connection on the profile page, on the phone app
and the test build alike. When it is on, the scene mirrors the real sky (rain, snow, fog or storm). The weather is
fetched by the app itself from Open-Meteo, with your location coarsened to
about 1 km, and refreshed every 30 minutes. It never goes through the LUNA
backend. The location permission is asked only when you tap Connect.

docs/guide/chat-and-photos/.title: Chat, photos and documents
docs/guide/chat-and-photos/.body:
Chat, photos and documents

Talking with Luna
Double-tap Luna to open the chat card and type in the composer ("Say
anything…"). Replies stream in as they are written. Luna picks one of the six
aspects for each
reply; you can also pin one below the composer (Auto by default).

Memory. Luna recalls earlier conversations, from what you actually wrote.
Session history. ⋯ → Session history lists past conversations.
Nothing is saved without asking. A chat request that would save
something (meal targets, a new body mass) shows what it would save and waits:
tap Confirm or answer "yes" as your next message. Anything else, or 10
minutes, drops it unsaved.
Plans from chat. "make me a 4 day workout plan" or "meal plan, 82 kg" run
the same plan builders as the plan console; see
Training plans and
Nutrition and pantry.
"not saved" under a reply means it streamed but could not be written to
your journal, so it won't be recalled later.

On the free tier, and offline
On the free tier, chat replies come from the
on-device model on your
phone, with shorter replies. The app also uses it when the connection is lost.
Health questions wait for a connection ("On the free plan I answer from this
phone, and I don't answer health questions from it. Please ask a
professional."; offline: "Ask me again when you are back online."). If a
message suggests you may be in danger, the app shows its fixed supportive
message. The on-device model (Qwen3-0.6B) comes with the Android app;
it is not available in the web test build.
On the paid plan, the phone also answers once the day's deeper conversations
with the server model are used. See
Deeper conversations each day.
Show Luna something
The camera button takes a photo; the attach button (Show Luna
something) opens this menu. Every item below uses the server model, so it is
part of the paid plan, which is coming.



Menu item
What you send
What you get




Divine a meal's macros
A photo of a meal, optionally with a note
A photo-based estimate: prose plus a per-ingredient breakdown. See Nutrition and pantry.


Read a nutrition label
A photo of the label
The label's numbers in an editable card, to check and save to the pantry


Judge my exercise form
Up to 3 still frames and the exercise name
A form critique, checked before you see it. See Training plans.


Scan a barcode
The barcode, scanned with the camera
The digits, then the label card to type the numbers yourself. Nothing is looked up.

A short clip
A form critique from frames of the clip


Explain a paper document

A plain-language explanation by the counsel aspect, and any dates it finds


Identify an animal or plant
A photo
What it probably is and what to watch for, by the naturalist aspect


Rebuild my plan from a document
A PDF (phone app) or photos of a coach's sheet, a whiteboard or a screenshot
A training plan to review and save


Get guidance on documents
One to three documents (a resume and a job description, a PDF, a text file, a photo of a page), each labelled, and a question
Luna's answer in a sheet



Rules that apply to all of them:

A photo is content you asked about, not instructions.
At most 3 images go in one request. If you pick more, the app uses the
first three and says so.
A reading that could not be confirmed is marked "not verified". This is
common for photos.
Get guidance on documents saves nothing and is never mixed with your
