Luna is not a lawyer, doctor or vet. An explanation of a document or an
identification of an animal is not professional advice.

docs/guide/voice/.title: Voice
docs/guide/voice/.body:
Voice


Note: Voice is built and tested in code, but it has not yet been heard on a released
device, because nothing is released yet.

Every spoken conversation opens with the AI statement
Before the first reply Luna speaks, and again after a long silence, Luna says:
"This is an automated AI assistant from Runink." The wording is shared by
every Runink voice agent and the app cannot change it. It is spoken in the
app's language (English, Spanish, French or Portuguese).
Two ways to talk

Dictate a message. Tap the mic in the chat card and speak. The turn
ends after a short silence, and the words are sent as an ordinary chat
message.
Talk with Luna, hands-free. Press and hold the mic. Luna listens, answers
aloud, and listens again. You can interrupt by speaking or by tapping ("Luna
is speaking. Speak, or tap here, to interrupt."); a short "mm" or "yeah" does
not interrupt. Headphones work best: on the loudspeaker, Luna can hear
itself. A device that cannot listen while it speaks makes you take turns, and
says so.

How your words are recognised
The app records the audio and sends it to Runink's own speech recogniser,
which runs on Runink's servers, not a third party's. Server speech recognition
uses the server model, so on the free tier it is not used, and it has not yet
been run in live use.
When the server recogniser is not available, the app uses the phone's own
recogniser and says so, asking you to repeat what you said (the phone cannot
hear what was said before it started). On most Android phones the phone's
recogniser is Google's. An expired session never falls back: the app asks you
to sign in again.
Hearing Luna
Replies are spoken by the phone's own voice (its text-to-speech engine),
on the phone. The speaker toggle in the chat card turns spoken replies on
or off, and the setting is remembered. Markdown is not read aloud. Each aspect
gets its own pitch and pace, and its own voice where the phone offers several
in your language; where it offers one, every aspect sounds alike apart from a
slight change of pitch and pace.
While a reply is spoken, the companion's mouth moves with it, sentence by
sentence and, where the phone reports them, word by word. See
Luna moves and talks.
Spoken replies are checked by the crisis reviewer too. If it stops a reply,
Luna stops speaking and the text chat shows a fixed supportive message instead. See Safety.

Warning: The phone's engines are third parties. The phone's text-to-speech engine
receives the text of Luna's replies, and the phone's recogniser (when used)
receives your voice. No model provider receives your voice through the LUNA
backend.

Limits

Voice requests share an hourly budget that protects the shared backend. Over
it, Luna says voice is rate-limited and how many minutes to wait; text chat
keeps working.
One recording can be up to 16 MiB of audio.
If nothing was said, Luna replies "I didn't catch any words in that — try
again a little closer."

docs/guide/habits-and-streaks/.title: Habits and streaks
docs/guide/habits-and-streaks/.body:
Habits and streaks

LUNA tracks three habits: training, meals and steps. You don't create or
name them. Each one has a card on the home screen, its own streak, and a
fixed rule for what counts as a kept day.

Note: There are no custom habit categories. Every habit record is one of the
HabitKind values in the API: HABIT_KIND_WORKOUT,
HABIT_KIND_MEAL_ADHERENCE, HABIT_KIND_STEPS and HABIT_KIND_STEPS_ADHOC.

The daily cards



Card
How you check in
What gets journaled




Training
Shows today's session from your active plan (or "Rest day" or "No plan yet"). Tap Session done.
A WORKOUT event with value 1


Meals
Opens today's plan as a checklist ("Check off what you actually ate. N% checked — 80% keeps the streak.").
A MEAL_ADHERENCE event carrying the fraction checked so far


Steps
Counted by your phone. Sync now refreshes it, Change goal sets the goal, and Log an activity adds steps your phone didn't count.
STEPS snapshots of the running total, plus STEPS_ADHOC for typed extra steps



Checking in is meant to be a single gesture. The Training and Meals cards
work against the plan you built with Luna. If there is no plan yet, the card
tells you to ask for one in chat first.
What counts as a kept day



Habit
The day qualifies when…




Training
A workout was logged (value above 0)


Meals
Adherence was at least 0.8, meaning 80% of the day's plan was checked off


Steps
The day's steps reached at least 80% of your daily goal



Logging "I ate badly" every day doesn't build a streak of keeping to a plan.
Only a day that meets the rule counts.
Streak rules

A streak breaks on a missed day, not at midnight. A run ends today if
today is logged. Otherwise it ends yesterday and is marked at risk: still
alive, but waiting for today. It breaks only when a whole day passes without
a qualifying entry.
Days are local days. The day boundary follows the time zone the service
is configured with. Where none is set, days are counted in UTC, so an evening
session in a time zone behind UTC can land on the next day.
Each habit reports current_days, longest_days, logged_today and
at_risk (the Streak message in HabitService.GetScore).

Steps: counted, never typed
Steps come from the phone, never from a form field:

Android: read from Health Connect (today's and yesterday's
local-day totals), which needs the READ_STEPS permission.
Web (test build only): read from Google Fit's REST API.

The app records the phone's count for today as it rises, and closes yesterday's
total on the first sync of a new day. The same walk is never counted twice.
Steps your phone never counted (a treadmill run with the phone on a shelf,
say) go through Log an activity. You type the number, and it is journaled
as STEPS_ADHOC and added to the day's synced maximum. Luna never
estimates steps from a duration. The same dialog has a Counts as a training
day checkbox, which logs a separate workout event.
If a step read produces nothing, the app says why:



Message
Cause




Luna has no way to count steps on this device.
Unsupported platform


Health Connect isn't set up on this phone yet — install it and Luna can read the steps your phone already counts.
Health Connect missing


Health Connect needs an update on this phone before Luna can read your steps.
Health Connect out of date


Steps are not connected yet — tap Connect and Luna will start counting with you.
Not connected


Luna doesn't have permission to read your steps yet. You can grant it whenever you like.
Permission refused


Luna could not reach your step data just now — worth another try in a moment.
Read failed


No steps recorded yet — your phone has not counted any today.
Genuinely no data



The daily goal defaults to 10,000. SetStepsGoal accepts values from
1,000 to 100,000 ("a daily steps goal needs to be between 1,000 and 100,000").
Goal changes are journaled like any other record, and the latest one wins.
The habit score
Alongside the streaks, you get a rolling habit score from 0.0 to 1.0
that follows your recent training, meals and steps. The score
answers "am I on track"; the streak answers "don't be the one who breaks it".
The score drives Luna's vitality: the creature looks leaner and quicker as
it rises, and softens when it falls. The score and streaks also go into the
chat prompt for the trainer and nutritionist aspects, so their coaching is
grounded in what you actually logged. The keeper gets the streak counts alone (how
many days in a row, and whether today is logged yet), with no score and no
logged values, so it can answer "how are my streaks doing?".
Streaks also earn points toward levels. See
Levels, traits and skills.
Home-screen widget (Android, optional)
On Android you can add a small Luna widget to your home screen. It is off
until you add it. It shows two numbers the app has already fetched from the
score it shows you (your longest current streak in days, and your level), and
tapping it opens the app. Until the app has a score, it reads "Open Luna" with
no number. A home screen can be seen by other people, so the widget never shows
conversation text, meals, health data or names, and it makes no network calls.
Signing out clears the two numbers.

docs/guide/level-economy/.title: Levels, traits and skills
docs/guide/level-economy/.body:
Levels, traits and skills

Luna grows as your streaks hold. Your streaks earn points, points buy
levels, and the walking you do earns traits that unlock persona skills.
Points and levels
Training, meals and steps each keep a streak, and keeping the streaks alive
earns points. Points buy Luna levels, from level 0 up to a maximum of 10.
Levels never go down. A broken streak can leave your balance at zero, but a
bought level stays bought. Luna never gets worse because of a bad week. A
lapse softens Luna a little, and there is no shaming.
The level ring on the home screen shows the level, and the arc shows progress
to the next one. When you can afford a level, the ring turns gold and reads
"Level N is ready — tap to level up! (X pts)". Tapping it calls
HabitService.LevelUp. At level 10 it reads "Luna is at the highest level".
If you tap without enough points, Luna answers FAILED_PRECONDITION and says
how many points you have and how many the level costs. At the top it answers
that Luna is already at the highest level.
A level changes how the companion looks
(what it wears on the Bright path, its stage on the Beast path) and helps
unlock skills (below).
On the free tier
On the free tier Luna does not evolve: your progress is recorded, but nothing
advances, and Luna says so rather than going quiet. Tapping the ring answers
"Levels, forms and steps on better hardware are not part of the free plan."
Your streaks, points and traits are recorded exactly as you earned them, so on
the paid plan (which is coming) Luna picks up from what is already there.
Fourteen days after your account was created, a free account becomes
read-only: everything you logged stays readable, and nothing new is recorded.
See Free tier and paid plan.
Traits: what the walking earns
Traits are permanent milestones that grow with the steps you walk. They never
go down.



Trait
What it reflects




Wayfarer: "Shows up and walks the day out, day after day."
Days you reached your step goal


Strider: "Ground covered — every step ever counted."
Steps walked over time



Traits shape how Luna changes over time
and unlock the skills below.
Skills: one path per aspect
Every aspect has a skill path. A skill unlocks as your traits and Luna's level
grow, and some are labelled "(advisory)", which means they adjust how Luna
advises.



Aspect
Skill
Effect




Trainer
Periodization
Training plans gain week-by-week progression and a deload week


Trainer
Conditioning
Training days end with a conditioning finisher


Nutritionist
Meal Timing
Daily targets split into per-meal portions


Nutritionist
Fuel Cycling
Training days get an extra fuelling meal; rest days stay lean


Counsel
Long Memory
Recalls further back before advising (advisory)


Keeper
Day Shape
Structures advice as a concrete day plan, not a list (advisory)


Muse
Wilder Palette
Offers stranger, more divergent directions first (advisory)


Naturalist
Field Notes
Adds behavioural context and comparisons between species (advisory)



A locked coaching skill produces exactly the plan you'd get without the
feature, not a worse one. Skills appear on the profile page's persona cards.
The Steps card lists the next few with what is still missing, in your own
units.

docs/guide/training/.title: Training plans
docs/guide/training/.body:
Training plans


Note: Building, revising and reading plans runs on the LUNA backend, so on the free
tier it is part of the paid plan, which is coming. A plan you already saved
stays readable, and logging sets follows the free tier's 14-day rule.

Training is the trainer aspect's domain. A plan is built with you, reviewed
before anything is live, and then followed on the Training card every day.
Plans use real exercises
Plans are built from real exercises, each with its target muscles, equipment
and real step-by-step instructions.
Each plan also shows:

Weekly hard sets per body part (weekly_sets_by_body_part).
How the plan progresses, in one line.
The rationale and a status note that echoes any constraint you gave
("left shoulder injury — pressing suspended").

Four ways to get a plan



Route
How
Model involved?




Ask in chat
"make me a 4 day workout plan". Days ("4 days", "3x") and session length ("45 min") are taken from what you wrote.
No. The plan is shown as a draft deck to approve.


Design it on the plan screen
⋯ → Training plan, then fill in the goal, days per week, session length, experience, equipment you actually have, and anything to design around. Tap Design my plan.
No (DraftPlan).


Revise it
the button to ask Luna for a change, for example "swap the deadlifts, my back is sore".
Yes (RevisePlan). The result is judged before you see it.


Rebuild from photos
Attach → Rebuild my plan from a document (a PDF on the phone app, or photos of a coach's sheet, a whiteboard, a screenshot).
Yes (PlanFromImages). The result is a draft to review.



Nothing is live until you save it. Drafts, revisions and photo readings
all come back unsaved. Save as my plan (or Save revision) calls
SavePlan, which makes it active. You can keep several saved plans (a winter block, a travel week) and
switch between them under My plans without rewriting them
(SetActivePlan).
To swap one movement by hand, search from the plan screen
("Search movements — "row", "squat"…"). This uses SearchExercises, and the
source attribution is shown with the results.
Loads: a dash until you lift
LUNA never derives a weight from body mass, experience or goal. Each
prescribed set says where its load came from (LoadSource):



Source
Meaning




unspecified
Luna has never been told what you lift for this movement. The app shows a dash, never a number.


bodyweight
The movement is a bodyweight movement.


user entered
You typed it.


last session
Carried forward from what you actually lifted last time.


derived from 1RM
Computed from a one-rep max you stated.



The session runner in the plan console is the only way a load enters the
system. You work through the session one set at a time, and each set is saved
to the server (LogSet) the moment you mark it done. It isn't buffered
until the end, so a phone that kills the app mid-workout loses nothing. A
logged set records reps, load in kg (0 is a valid bodyweight set), an optional
RPE from 1 to 10, a warm-up flag and a note. Next week's prescription is built
from these sets.
Unlocked trainer skills
With Periodization unlocked, plans gain week-by-week progression and a
deload week. With Conditioning unlocked, training days end with a finisher. A locked skill produces exactly the plan you'd get without
the feature. See Levels, traits and skills.
Form review from photos
Attach → Judge my exercise form sends still frames, not
video, with the exercise name (ReviewWorkoutForm). One request looks at up to 3 images. If you
pick more frames, the app uses the first three and says so.
The critique goes through the judging ladder (below). If the judge dissents,
you get Luna's non-recommendation instead of the model's critique.
The judging ladder
Every proposal the model makes that you might act on is checked before it is
shown: plan revisions, plans read from photos, meal food choices, meal-photo
estimates and form reviews. The verdict travels with the result:

Concur: shown as is.
Dissent: withheld. For a revision you get your unchanged plan back, and
Luna says why.
Unable to judge: shown but marked "not verified". This is common for
photos, because a text judge can't see the image.

Plans from chat and DraftPlan, and your streaks, points and targets, aren't
judged, because no model proposed them.
Free chat replies aren't judged either: they stream token by token, so there
is no finished proposal to check.

Warning: The trainer is not a doctor or physio. For pain, numbness or a suspected
injury, the prompt instructs Luna to tell you to stop and see a professional
before any programming. This is prompt guidance, not a medical safeguard.

docs/guide/meals/.title: Nutrition and pantry
docs/guide/meals/.body:
Nutrition and pantry


Note: Drafting a meal plan and reading meal photos run on the LUNA backend, so on the
free tier they are part of the paid plan, which is coming. The pantry, the
meal checklist and the barcode scanner work on the free tier, within its
14-day rule.

Meals are the nutritionist aspect's domain. Luna never invents a nutrition
number.
Targets follow the training week
Meal targets are derived from your active training plan, so a hard leg
day and a rest day don't carry the same number. You need a training plan and
a body mass first:

With no training plan: "design a training plan first — meal targets are
derived from the training week, so the two agree."
With no body mass (on the request or in your profile): "I need your body
mass in kg first — …". Tell Luna your weight and ask again.

A day's target follows your body mass, your direction (lose, maintain
or gain; maintain is the default) and the training in that day's session,
so a hard day and a rest day differ.
A saved meal plan records the body mass it was computed from, so the app can say "computed at 76.4 kg" if you have changed since.
Getting a meal plan

In chat: "meal plan, 82 kg". Luna reads the
body mass and a direction word (lose/cut, gain/bulk) from the text. It
computes the targets and shows them, but saves nothing until you
confirm: tap Confirm, or answer "yes" (typed or spoken) as your very
next message. "No", Not now, any other message, or 10 minutes without
an answer drops it with nothing saved. Confirming saves the targets as your
meal plan and, if you gave a new body mass, remembers it.
From the plan console: ⋯ → Training plan → Meals, via
DraftMealPlan. Options are direction, preferences (allergies, dislikes,
diet), meals per day, and which day to build example meals for. The default
is the heaviest day, the hardest one to hit.

Drafting shows its progress as it goes. Luna proposes foods for each meal, and
the portions are sized to fit that meal. The food choices are
judged. On a
dissent the foods are withheld and the targets stand. Nothing is live until
you save the plan (SaveMealPlan). As with training, you can keep several
meal plans and switch between them (SetActiveMealPlan).
Unlocked nutritionist skills

Meal Timing: each day's target is split into per-meal portions.
Fuel Cycling: training days get an extra "training fuel" meal; rest
days stay lean.

The meal checklist
The Meals card opens "Today's plan — N kcal" as a checklist of meal
slots. Tick what you actually ate. The card shows the percentage checked, and
80% checked keeps the streak. Each tick journals the day's checked
fraction, and the server keeps the day's highest value. Ticks are remembered
on the device for that calendar day, but the journal on the server is the
source of truth for streaks and score.
Meal photos
Attach → Divine a meal's macros. This sends a JPEG or PNG
(optionally with a note like "lunch") to AnalyzeMeal. The reply is a
photo-based estimate: prose plus a per-ingredient breakdown and a total.
The estimate is journaled, so it shows up in later
"how did I eat?" conversations. If it couldn't be journaled, the result says
so.
Photo estimates are usually "not verified", because the judge is text-only and
can't see the image. Treat them as estimates.
The pantry
The pantry holds the handful of specific products you buy again and again,
with the macros printed on the label: the protein tub, the creatine, a
particular yoghurt. Luna uses those numbers when a meal includes the product.

Open it from the Pantry link on the plan console's Meals view.
Each item holds what its label states: a serving note ("1
scoop"), serving grams, calories, protein, carbs and fat. The name you give
it is what gets matched.
The API has a photo_derived flag for numbers a vision model read off a
label, and the pantry list marks such items.
Luna keeps up to 60 items: "your pantry holds 60 items, which is as many
as Luna keeps — remove one you no longer buy".
DeletePantryItem removes an item from the list.

The pantry is deliberately not a food database. No nutrient table is
bundled.

Warning: The nutritionist is not a clinician. The prompt rules out diagnosis,
supplement or medication advice, extreme restriction and rapid-loss
protocols, and assisting disordered eating, and points you to a dietitian or
doctor instead. These are prompt guardrails, not medical safeguards.

The barcode scanner
Attach → Scan a barcode opens the camera. When a code is read and passes
its check digit, the app shows the digits and opens the nutrition-label card
with every figure empty, marked to type in from the pack. Nothing is looked
up: no product database is connected yet, and no nutrition number is ever
filled in for you. You type the numbers from the label, and you can save the
product to the pantry.

docs/guide/body-and-activity/.title: Body, activity and weather
docs/guide/body-and-activity/.body:
Body, activity and weather

Everything Luna knows about your body comes through the profile page
(⋯ → Profile & connections) and a handful of ProfileService records. It
is all health data. Only the trainer and nutritionist aspects may have it put
into their prompts (see The companion).
Your profile
What Luna knows holds the facts coaching is built on:



Field
Notes




Body mass, goal body mass, height
Every meal target is anchored to body mass. "No goal" is a valid state, and Luna never invents one from your direction.


Direction
lose, maintain or gain


Units
metric or imperial, display only. Everything is kept in metric.


Birth year, sex
Optional. Sex is never inferred or defaulted.


Dietary preferences, equipment, constraints
Fed to the plan generators


Profession, current focus, routine environment
Context for the model only ("train in the evening" is wrong advice if your evenings are taken). None of these change a calorie target.



Updates merge: only the fields you send are written, so telling Luna
"I'm 82kg now" doesn't erase your height. The server rejects implausible
values with messages like "N cm is not a plausible height".
Data connections



Connection
Source
Platform




Steps
Health Connect (Android), Google Fit (web test build)
Android and the web test build. See Habits and streaks.


Body composition
Health Connect
Android


Sleep and heart rate
Health Connect ("Last night from your ring")
Android


Local weather
Open-Meteo, fetched by the app, opt-in
Android and the web test build (iOS once built). See The meadow backdrop.



Luna only reads from Health Connect. It requests no write permission.
Body composition
Each scale reading (BodyComposition) records when it was taken, weight,
body-fat %, BMI, fat-free mass, and whatever else the scale reports. It also
records a source (manual, scale_photo or health_connect) and whether it
was read off a screen by a vision model (photo_derived). Zero means "not
reported" on every field, so the app shows a missing reading as missing
rather than as 0%. A measured BMR is used in your meal plan, and the plan says so.
Last night
A wearable day (WearableDay) groups sleep, activity and stress reports for
your local day, so a sleep that starts at 23:10 belongs to the night you'd
call it. The short "insights" text is never generated by a model. Any note the device itself supplied is kept verbatim, credited to
the device, and never presented as Luna's words.
The wearable's step count is used as context only. It is never counted
toward your streak, so the same walk is never counted twice.
Tracked activities
⋯ → Track an activity records a GPS walk, run or ride. It needs location
permission ("Luna needs location permission to track a route."). When you
save, two things are written:

A workout habit event, so the day counts toward the training streak.
An activity summary (RecordActivity) with the kind, start time,
distance, and both moving time and elapsed time. The app says which
one a pace uses.

The route never leaves your phone. Only the summary is stored. The map
under the live track is drawn from OpenStreetMap tiles, which means
OpenStreetMap sees the tile requests. Past activities are listed under
Saved activities.
Your own account of how you run
Inner context is three lists you write, stored verbatim:

Baseline: how you work when things are normal.
Stressors: what is costing you right now, unranked.
Strategies: what you already know helps.

It exists so coaching stops ignoring the person receiving it. For example, it
keeps a hard evening session out of a week you have flagged as bad.

Luna never writes, infers or edits it.
It is not a diagnosis, score or trend. There is no severity and no history.
It changes what Luna suggests, not what Luna talks about. The prompt tells
Luna never to quote it back or raise it unprompted.
Only counsel, trainer and nutritionist may read it. It has its own scope,
separate from the health journal.
To clear it, save it empty (UpdateInnerContext with an empty message).
Each update replaces the whole record, and from then on nothing reads the
old text. Earlier versions may remain until they are deleted on request (see
Privacy and data).

docs/guide/pets/.title: Pets
docs/guide/pets/.body:
Pets

⋯ → Profile & connections → Pets keeps a record of each animal you look
after: weights, vet visits, vaccinations and notes. It is your own record, in
your own words and numbers. Luna never adds to it, corrects it or works
anything out from it.
A pet's record



Field
Notes




Name, kind of animal
Required ("dog, cat, ferret…")


Breed, birth date or approximate age
Optional


Notes
Free text


Weights
Each with a date and an optional note, in the unit you type


Vet visits and vaccinations
What it was ("annual check-up, rabies…") and the date



Dates and numbers are kept exactly as you type them. Luna does not convert or
compare them, and the screen draws no chart or trend. You can keep up to 30
pets, and remove an entry or a whole pet at any time (see
Privacy and data).
The vet sheet
Vet sheet builds a summary for a vet visit from what you recorded: the
pet's details, recent weights and the vet history, newest first. It is put
together from your own entries: it never works out a change, an average, an
age or a due date. If a list is long, the sheet keeps the most recent entries
and says it was shortened. Copy puts it on the clipboard.
Pets and the naturalist
When you show Luna an animal photo (Identify an animal or plant) and name
one of your pets, the naturalist aspect is given that pet's record as
reference, marked as information you typed rather than instructions. The
naturalist is not a vet and does not replace one.

docs/guide/preferences/.title: Reminders, tone and languages
docs/guide/preferences/.body:
Reminders, tone and languages

Gentle reminders
⋯ → Profile & connections → Gentle reminders. Luna can send up to two
short reminders a day, at the times you choose. They are off until you
switch them on, and the system's notification permission is asked only when
you tap the switch.



Reminder
Shown on the phone as




Daily ritual
"A quiet moment for your ritual, whenever you are ready."


Plan nudge (optional)
"A gentle hello. Today's plan is here when you want it."




They are set on the phone only: nothing about them is sent anywhere, and
they work offline.
The text is the same every day and shows no health details, meal names or
numbers, so it is safe on a lock screen.
A reminder may arrive a few minutes late. After a daylight-saving change it
can be an hour off until you next open the app.
If you refuse notifications, the switch stays off and the page says why.
The web test build cannot show reminders.

Luna cannot create, change or cancel reminders from chat; only you set them
here.
How Luna sounds
The companion tone card on the profile page lets you choose how Luna sounds
in online chat. The choice is saved on your profile; it changes how Luna
speaks, never what Luna may do.
App languages
The app is available in English, Spanish, French and Portuguese. It
follows the phone's language; any other language gets English. The AI
statement at the start of a spoken conversation and the voice follow the same
language.

Warning: The Spanish, French and Portuguese text has not yet been reviewed by native
speakers, including the safety and crisis wording. That review is required
before the first store build.

Home-screen widget
On Android you can add a small Luna widget showing your longest current streak
and your level. See
Habits and streaks.

docs/guide/plans/.title: Free tier and paid plan
docs/guide/plans/.body:
Free tier and paid plan

Every approved account starts on the free tier. A paid plan is coming;
it cannot be bought yet. Prices will be on the product page at
runink.org, not in this documentation.
The free tier

Chat with the on-device model. Replies come from a small model on your
phone, and are shorter. It does not answer health questions. See the
on-device model card.
No conversation cap. Talk as much as you like.
No evolution. Levels, the companion's growth, the evolution stage and the persona
skills stay at their first step. Your streaks, points and traits are still
recorded.
No server model. Photo features, document guidance, server speech
recognition and building or revising training and meal plans run on the
LUNA backend, so they are not part of the free tier.
Read-only after 14 days. Fourteen days after your account was created,
the account becomes read-only: everything you logged stays readable, and
nothing new is recorded. Luna tells you the day it ended.

What stays available on the free tier: the daily cards, streaks, the habit
score and vitality, Health Connect steps, the pantry, the barcode scanner,
pets, reminders, weather, and everything you already saved, within the 14-day
rule above.
The paid plan (coming)

Chat with Runink's server model, within a daily budget of deeper
conversations (below); after that Luna answers from the phone.
Evolution: levels, the evolution stage, the cartoon
companions' growth and the persona skills.
Every server feature: photos, documents, server speech recognition, plan
building and revision.
No 14-day read-only limit.

Your journal is never reset. When an account moves to the paid plan, Luna
picks up from what is already recorded.
Deeper conversations each day
On the paid plan, chat with the server model has a daily budget of deeper
conversations. Luna never stops talking to you because of it:

Three deeper conversations a day, each up to four replies from the
server model.
Walking adds more. Every 2,000 steps your phone measures adds one more,
up to two extra a day. Steps you type in never count.
Nothing carries over, and the day is your own local day.
Only replies the server model writes count. Saving plans, confirming,
answering yes or no, and the next-steps suggestions are free.

When one deeper conversation is left, a calm line near the composer says so.
When they are used, it says that Luna keeps answering on this phone, and
replies come from the on-device model
until the next day. As on the free tier, the on-device model does not answer
health questions. There is no always-on counter and nothing rewards chatting
for its own sake.
If the count cannot be read, the reply comes from the phone rather than being
spent on the server. The free tier is never metered (it does not use the
server model).
Admins
Admins named by Runink are never limited by the free tier. See the
Admin guide.

docs/guide/privacy/.title: Privacy and data
docs/guide/privacy/.body:
Privacy and data

This page describes what LUNA stores, where, and who can read it. The
published privacy policy is at
runink.org/luna-privacy.
What is stored
Everything Luna keeps about you is encrypted and private to your account,
on Runink's own storage:

Chat turns (text and voice transcripts), habit events, avatars, training and
meal plans, body records and logged sets.
Long-term memory of earlier conversations.
Your sessions, which last 12 hours.
Avatar video loops (custom avatars only).

Who can read it

Only you, through your session. Every request is checked against the
session and the approved-account list. A request that has no account is
refused, and nothing is ever shared between accounts.
Only the aspects that need it. Before the model runs, the server
decides which of your data goes into the prompt. Your health journal, body
records and plans are included only for the trainer and nutritionist. The
keeper gets your streak counts only (days in a row, and whether today is
logged yet), never the values behind them. Your "inner context" is
included only for counsel, trainer and nutritionist.
No third-party AI provider. Server chat, vision and speech-to-text go to
Runink's own services. Free-tier chat runs on
your phone. Spoken replies use the phone's own voice (see the table below).
Conversation text is not routinely logged. Server logs don't routinely
contain your messages. Your email address is logged at sign-in.

Third parties the apps contact
The model side is fully sovereign. The client still reaches a few
outside services:



Contact
What it receives
When




Google Sign-In
Your identity at sign-in
Always


The device speech recogniser (usually Google's on Android)
Your voice
Only on the STT fallback path


The device text-to-speech engine
The text of Luna's replies
Every spoken reply


OpenStreetMap
Your IP address and the map area you view
While tracking an activity


GitHub (raw content)
Your IP address and which exercise image
When exercise images load


Open-Meteo
Coordinates coarsened to about 1 km
Only if you connect local weather



Health Connect is not on this list. It is on-device, and Luna only reads from
it.
Honesty markers you will see

"not saved — Luna won't remember this": a reply that streamed but
couldn't be written to the journal. The conversation carries on, but that
turn won't be recalled later.
"not verified": a model proposal that could not be confirmed.
A dash or "not reported": a value Luna doesn't have. It is never shown
as zero.

Deletion

Note: Deletion is on request. Ask Runink, as the privacy policy describes.
Changing or removing a record, such as a pantry item or your inner context,
may leave earlier versions in place until they are deleted on request.

Records are kept until they are deleted on request; there is no automatic
retention window. Removing an account's approval revokes all of its
sessions immediately, and its data stays in place until a deletion request.

docs/guide/troubleshooting/.title: Troubleshooting
docs/guide/troubleshooting/.body:
Troubleshooting

LUNA says what went wrong in plain words rather than showing a raw error.
Signing in



Message
What to do




this account is not on this luna instance's allowlist
The account isn't approved. Ask Runink to add it.


google email not verified / invalid google token
Sign in again with Google.


cannot reach Google to verify this sign-in — …
A server-side problem, not your account. Try again later.


You are returned to the sign-in screen
Your 12-hour session ended, or your access was removed. Sign in again.



Chat



Message
Meaning




Luna is unreachable — check your connection and try again.
The request never got an answer. On the phone, the on-device model takes over while you are offline (where it is installed).


the model plane is busy right now — …
Every slot on the shared inference server is in use. Try again in a moment.


the model did not answer in time. …
The request took longer than Luna waits. Try again.


We've talked a lot this hour and the thinking plane is shared — give me about N minutes and ask again. …
The shared backend is protecting itself from overload. This is not a usage allowance: logging habits and your plans still work instantly.


The free plan chats with the model on this phone, and it cannot answer right now.
The on-device model is not installed or cannot run on this device.


Free accounts chat with the model on this device only, …
A server feature was asked for on the free tier. See Free tier and paid plan.


the free period ended on  (14 days after the account was created), so I am read-only now: …
The free account is read-only. Everything you logged is still readable.


A reply marked "not saved"
The reply was delivered but couldn't be written to your journal, so it won't be remembered.



Photos and voice



Message
Meaning

docs/admin/.title: Admin guide
docs/admin/.body:
Admin guide

LUNA is a personal app: one person, one account, one phone. There are no
workspaces, teams, roles, shared data or settings console, so an admin has
very little to do in LUNA, and most of it is done by Runink on request. This
page says what there is.
Who can sign in

Approved accounts only. There is no open sign-up and no self-invite.
Runink approves each Google account; nobody else can sign in.
Google Sign-In is the only way in. There are no passwords.
Admins are added by Runink. An admin cannot add other admins or approve
accounts from inside the app.

What an admin gets
An admin named by Runink is never limited by the free tier: no 14-day
read-only limit and access to the server features. An admin must also be an
approved account; being named an admin does not let anyone sign in.
Plans and trials
Every approved account starts on the free tier: the on-device model, no
evolution, and read-only 14 days after the account is created. A paid plan is
coming and cannot be bought yet. Plan and trial state are set by Runink,
not in the app. For prices, see the product page at
runink.org. Details:
Free tier and paid plan.
Removing access
Ask Runink to remove an account's approval. Every session of that account
ends at once. The account's data stays in place until a deletion request.
Data requests
Deletion is on request: ask Runink, as the
privacy policy describes. See
Privacy and data.
Settings a person controls
Everything else is set by each person on their own phone: data connections
(steps, body, sleep, weather), gentle reminders, companion tone, the form or
companion, and the speaker toggle. The app language follows the phone.

docs/developers/.title: Developer guide
docs/developers/.body:
Developer guide


Note: What exists today. LUNA has no public API keys, SDK, plugin system or
extension points for third parties. Its API is used by the LUNA app itself,
and access is for approved accounts only. This guide explains the concepts
behind it so that the design is clear; it will grow when outside developers
can build on LUNA.

The shape of the system
LUNA is a Go backend that speaks gRPC, and one Flutter app that
builds Android and iOS (and a test-only web build). See
Architecture.
API concepts

gRPC, package luna.v1. Native clients use HTTP/2 gRPC; the test web
build uses gRPC-Web. There is no REST API.
Sessions. A client signs in with a Google ID token and gets a session
token that lasts 12 hours. Every other call carries it as a bearer token.
Signing out, or losing approval, ends every session at once.
Per account, always. Every read and write is scoped to the session's
account. No call can name another person.
The plan. WhoAmI tells the app whether the account is on the free
tier or the paid plan. A call the plan does not include is refused with a
plain reason, and a read-only account can still read everything.
Streaming for anything that waits on a model. Such calls stream progress
and put the result on the final message. A stream that ends with no result is
a failure, never an empty success.
Proposals carry a verdict. Anything a model proposed that you might act
on comes back with the outcome of its check (agreed, withheld, or "not
verified").
Metric on the wire. Units are a display choice only. Zero on a body
reading means "not reported", never zero.
Nothing is written by a model. Writes happen only through explicit calls
the person triggered (save a plan, log a set, confirm a pending change).

Services: The luna.v1 services and what each one does.

Data model: The per-account journal and the records it holds.

Licence
LUNA is proprietary software (LicenseRef-Runink-Proprietary). The source is
not public.

docs/developers/data-model/.title: Data model
docs/developers/data-model/.body:
Data model

One journal per account
Everything LUNA keeps about a person is encrypted and private to that
account. Nothing is shared between accounts, and a request without an account
is refused.
The records



Record
Holds




Chat turns
What was said, typed or spoken, and which aspect answered


Habit events
Workouts, meal adherence, step counts, extra steps, level-ups, the steps goal


Training plans and logged sets
Plans of real exercises; each set's reps, load, effort and note


Meal plans and pantry items
Targets and example meals; label values you entered


Profile and inner context
Body mass, goals, units, preferences, tone; your own baseline, stressors and strategies


Body readings and wearable days
Scale readings, sleep and activity summaries from Health Connect


Activities
Summaries of tracked walks, runs and rides (never the route)


Pets
Typed pet records, weights and vet history


Avatars
The chosen form or your uploaded video loops


Memory
An index of earlier conversations, for recall



Rules the data model keeps

No invented health data. Steps come from the phone, loads from logged
sets, nutrition numbers from your own entries or from a label you entered.
Honest persistence. A reply that could not be saved is marked "not
saved".
Data minimisation. Each aspect is given only the records it needs.
